name: Ruins of Ravenwind
summary: In northern Feralas, harpies nest among the Ruins of Ravenwind as dragonkin watch the broken stone. The marble once belonged to an ancient Highborne city.

sections.title: Echoes of the Highborne
sections.body:
Before the Great Sundering, the Highborne ruled from Ravenwind at the height of their power. Like Dire Maul to the east, the kaldorei city was abandoned long ago.

Now foliage winds through broken arches and forgotten arcane altars. Northspring harpies roost there and prey on anything that wanders beneath the stone.

sections.title: A Confluence of Wild Dangers
sections.body:
Northspring harpies are not the only danger near Ravenwind. Fierce green dragonkin called the Jaedemir circle the central groves and waterways, guarding ancient arboreal sites.

Night elf explorers and solitary gnolls sometimes wander nearby. Lingering magic and wild predators can trap them among the ruins.

faq.q: Who built the Ruins of Ravenwind?
faq.answer: The Highborne, the aristocratic upper class of the ancient kaldorei, built Ravenwind millennia ago. After the Sundering, it fell into ruin, like Dire Maul and other elven monuments across Feralas.
Northspring harpies nest among the broken stonework, while dragonkin of the Jaedemir flight prowl the surrounding waters and central grove. They fiercely guard the local flora.

faq.q: Why does the Alliance visit this area?
faq.answer: Alliance scholars and sentinels at Feathermoon Stronghold send adventurers to seek lost arcane relics. They also use ancient altars to recharge powerful artifacts such as the Stave of Equinex.

angles.text: For the kaldorei, these ruins recall the reckless arcane empire that tore ancient Kalimdor apart. Harpies and wild beasts now foul the site.
From Feathermoon Stronghold, Alliance outposts keep watch on Ravenwind. Scouts seek potent magical relics before feral creatures or darker powers consume them.
